slides.title: Why the US, and why Amazon
K-beauty brands won 39% of the growth in US facial skincare since 2021, reaching $3.6B in 2025

claims.claim: 38.6% of the category's growth in 2021–25 went to K-beauty brands
K-beauty brands: sales grew 1.9 times in four years, while the whole category grew 22%
Share: K-beauty rose from 9.5% to 14.7% of US facial skincare, a segment still gaining ground
Not $5.2B: a 2026 trade-press figure also counts makeup and hair care; this deck uses the facial skincare figure

slides.title: Amazon is the way in: it carries 41% of K-beauty skincare sales, and 61% of K-beauty buyers shop there most

claims.claim: Amazon sells more US K-beauty skincare than specialty and mass retail together
evidence: Share of US K-beauty skincare sales by channel, 2025: Amazon 0.41; Specialty beauty retail 0.27; Mass retail 0.14; Brand websites (DTC) 0.12; Other 0.06

claims.claim: K-beauty buyers shop on Amazon and discover brands on social media, not in stores
evidence: Buy K-beauty on Amazon most often 0.61; Found last new brand on TikTok 0.38; Buy K-beauty at specialty retail most often 0.22; Found last new brand in a store 0.17
Survey of 1,200 US women aged 18–44 who bought facial skincare in the last six months; K-beauty buyers are a subset (size not reported)

slides.title: The pilot shows real demand, with monthly units up 89% in six months, but repeat purchase still trails the US benchmark

claims.claim: Units grew every month with only three SKUs and a cross-border seller
evidence: Pilot rating 4.5 stars from 2,140 reviews; the most common complaint (6% of reviews) was Korean-only label text, fixed by the US setup

claims.claim: Fewer first-time buyers come back than for a typical first-year brand
evidence: −2 pp
90-day repeat rate: Onsoo in Korea 0.48; US first-year benchmark 0.31; Onsoo US pilot 0.29

slides.title: Japan would return similar cash by 2030, but the US Amazon route builds nearly four times the revenue

claims.claim: The US route adds three to four times Japan's revenue in every year
evidence: Japan scale-up revenue 2027–30: 2.5; 4.5; 6; 7 ($M)

claims.claim: Both options stay far inside the cash cap and are cash-positive by 2030
evidence: Cumulative cash, deepest point (end-2027): US -1.94; Japan -1.05
Cumulative cash, end-2030: US 2.39975; Japan 1.8

claims.claim: With room for one launch in 2027, the US is the better use: Japan's market grows about 1.5% a year, and it does nothing for the US ambition

slides.title: Why not a retail-led launch
Of the two US routes, only Amazon-led stays inside the board's cash, payback and margin limits

claims.claim: A · Amazon-led (US): The only US route that fits / Its deepest outflow is about a tenth of the cap, and group margin stays above the floor in 2027
evidence: Revenue added 2030 $26.4M; deepest cumulative cash −$1.9M; cumulative cash end-2030 $2.4M; lowest group margin 9.5%

claims.claim: B · Retail-led (US): Fails all three limits, even on its own inputs
evidence: Revenue added 2030 $37.6M; deepest cumulative cash −$20.8M; cumulative cash end-2030 −$20.8M; lowest group margin 4.5%
Tests: ambition $40M US; cap −$18M; payback above $0; margin floor 8%

claims.claim: J · Japan scale-up: Safe, but small and outside the US
evidence: Revenue added 2030 $7M; deepest cumulative cash −$1.1M; cumulative cash end-2030 $1.8M; lowest group margin 10.1%

slides.title: Retail-led would consume $20.8M by 2030: retail marketing and field sales alone cost more than the route earns

claims.claim: retail marketing and field sales cost 1.3x all contribution Option B earns in 2027–30
evidence: Base US costs 8.4; One-time costs 2.4; Inventory 2.5532; Retail marketing 24; Field sales 6; Amazon contribution 17.2604; Retail contribution 5.29659; Cash consumed 20.7962 ($M)

claims.claim: Retail marketing and field sales: fixed at $7.5M a year, whatever the doors sell
Per door: each door earns about $1,766 of contribution a year at plan, against $12,500 of retail cost per door in 2027
Board limits: the total passes the $18M cap in 2029, and the 2027 loss cuts group margin to 4.5%, below the 8% floor
evidence: Amazon contribution includes the planning team's 1.3x halo on Option A volumes

slides.title: At Onsoo's awareness level, retail newcomers sell a median 2.6 units per door weekly, below the retailer's 4.0 minimum

claims.claim: The plan borrows sell-through from brands far better known than Onsoo
evidence: Median units per door per week: Below 10% 2.6; 10–20% 3.5; Above 20% 4.6; Planning assumption 4.5
Removal threshold after 12 months 4.0
Retail analytics firm, 2025, 46 brands; interquartile range below 10% awareness is 1.9–3.4 units

claims.claim: Below 10%: Onsoo's band, at 9% awareness among K-beauty buyers
Planning assumption: from successful newcomers only, 1.7 times Onsoo's band
10–20%: also misses the cut, so a 15% retail gate is too low
Retail-led cash, end-2030, at 2.6 units and no halo
evidence: Plan model; Amazon at Option A volumes

slides.title: The Amazon halo that props up retail-led rests on a correlation, not on evidence that retail drives Amazon sales

claims.claim: Brand strength drives both doors and Amazon sales
evidence: The memo's 0.71 correlation across 30 brands shows size, not cause
Strong brands win shelf space and sell more online
No before-and-after test of what doors did to Amazon sales
1.3x uplift Option B applies to every Amazon unit

claims.claim: The arrow runs from Amazon to retail
evidence: Saebom reached about $30M on Amazon before adding doors
Retailers recruit brands that already sell
38% of K-beauty buyers find new brands on TikTok, 17% in a store
300 doors Saebom added after scaling on Amazon

claims.claim: Without the halo, retail is a small revenue line
evidence: 1,000 doors at 4.5 units a week add $3.3M of revenue in 2030
The halo supplies 71% of Option B's 2030 lead over Amazon-led
That retail line costs $7.5M a year to run
8.7% of Option B's 2030 revenue comes from retail doors

claims.claim: Option B's case for retail is the halo, and the evidence offered for it does not show cause

slides.title: What Amazon-led depends on
Advertising is the largest cost in each $24 Amazon sale, and at plan it leaves Onsoo $4.73 of contribution

claims.claim: Ad cost is the one large line Onsoo controls
evidence: Price 24; Advertising (25% ACoS) 6; FBA fulfillment 5.1; Referral fee (15%) 3.6; Product, ex-factory 3.5; Freight 0.55; Duty (15%) 0.525; Contribution 4.725 ($ per unit)

claims.claim: Advertising: each percentage point of ACoS costs $0.24 a unit, 5% of the contribution
At the 32% agency benchmark: contribution falls to $3.05 a unit, 36% below plan
Fees and product: set by Amazon's rate card and the factory; a 25% tariff would add $0.35 of duty a unit, 7% of contribution

slides.title: Amazon-led pays back by 2030 only if ad costs average below 28.6% of sales, barely above the pilot's 28%

claims.claim: Payback rests on the ad cost the plan assumes away
evidence: Break-even average ACoS, 2027–30: 28.6% = (margin before ads − fixed costs) ÷ sales
$2.4M cash end-2030 at 25%; $67.4M Amazon sales 2027–30; 7 pp higher ACoS at 32%; −$2.3M cash end-2030 at 32%
ACoS in the pilot, small budget: 28%
Agency benchmark: median ACoS for skincare brands scaling from $5M to $20M a year on Amazon US (range 26%–38%)

claims.claim: At 25% (plan): assumes ad costs fall; agency data say they rise with scale
At 32%: outflow peaks at $3.2M, 18% of the cap: payback slips, the cap holds

slides.title: Amazon-first is the only route with a K-beauty success, yet two of the three brands that took it stayed small

claims.claim: Saebom: The sequence to copy / Retail came after Amazon scale, not before it
evidence: Amazon-first, 2022; About $30M US revenue; added 300 retail doors in 2025

claims.claim: Gaon Lab and Yeoreum: Same route, no scale: execution decided
evidence: Gaon Lab: Amazon-first, 2022; Below $5M US revenue
Yeoreum: Amazon-first, 2023; Below $5M US revenue

claims.claim: Mooncrest: Loss above Onsoo's $18M cap
evidence: Retail-first, 2023, 450 doors; Removed from shelves in 2025; estimated US loss of $21M

slides.title: How to proceed
No route reaches the $40M ambition by 2030 within the limits; Amazon-led gets two thirds of the way, to $26.4M

claims.claim: 66% of the $40M ambition reached in 2030 on the planning team's volumes
evidence: Board ambition, $40M

claims.claim: To reach $40M on Amazon: about 1.67 million units in 2030, 52% more than the plan
Retail-led is no shortcut: it gets closer only by breaking the cash cap, and 91% of its 2030 revenue is still Amazon
Restate $40M as a goal beyond 2030 and judge 2027–30 on payback and the retail gates

slides.title: The roadmap launches on Amazon in 2027 and holds retail back until both its sales and awareness gates are met

claims.claim: Roadmap: Board go; Tariff decision; ACoS review; Retail gate: sales above $10M and awareness above 20%
evidence: Setup: Entity, MoCRA, English labels
Amazon: Own account, seven SKUs; Scale to plan volumes
Brand building: TikTok and influencers, $0.7M a year
Retail: Test with one retailer, only if both gates are met

claims.claim: A 20% awareness gate, not 15%, is the only band where median sell-through clears the 4.0 cut
evidence: Sales gate from the CEO's hypothesis; Option A's planning volumes give $13.4M of Amazon sales in 2028
Awareness gate from Table 8: only brands above 20% aided awareness have a median above the 4.0 removal threshold

slides.title: Four guardrails would trigger a board review before the Amazon route drifts outside the board's limits

claims.claim: Ad cost: hold average ACoS at or below the pilot's level; review if it runs higher for two quarters
evidence: The guardrail that decides payback · Each percentage point of ACoS costs $0.24 a unit
28% pilot ACoS; payback by 2030 needs an average below 28.6%

claims.claim: Tariff: re-run the model on the mid-2027 duty decision and reprice if duty reaches 25%
evidence: 7.4% of contribution per unit lost if duty rises from 15% to 25%

claims.claim: Labels: ship only English-labeled units from launch, before ad spend scales
evidence: 6% of pilot reviews complained of Korean-only labels

claims.claim: Repeat: lift 90-day repeat to the US benchmark as the four added SKUs launch
evidence: 31% first-year US benchmark, compared with 29% in the pilot

slides.title: Next steps

normalized.recommendation: Approve a gated Amazon launch and move the $40M ambition beyond 2030: approve Option A, the four guardrails and the two retail gates (Amazon sales above $10M and awareness above 20%); restate $40M as a post-2030 goal; defer retail.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Chosen: "The only US route that fits / Its deepest outflow is about a tenth of the cap, and group margin stays above the floor in 2027"; payback needs ad costs below 28.6% of sales.

Rejected: "Fails all three limits, even on its own inputs"; consumes $20.8M by 2030 beyond the $18M cap; sell-through assumption borrowed from better-known brands; 1.3x Amazon halo rests on a correlation, not on cause.
Rejected: "Safe, but small and outside the US"; similar cash by 2030 but US route builds nearly four times the revenue; Japan's market grows about 1.5% a year and does nothing for the US ambition.
Rejected in favour of 20%: "10–20%: also misses the cut, so a 15% retail gate is too low".

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Synthetic benchmark data; every figure from the briefing pack
K-beauty buyers are a subset (size not reported) of the 1,200-person survey
US revenue = planning-team Amazon units × $24.00; Japan = planning-team incremental revenue (Table 7), no inventory build given
Group margin adds each option's operating result to the ex-US plan at 11.0% margin; setup and fixtures are expensed
At 25% (plan): assumes ad costs fall; agency data say they rise with scale
At the 32% benchmark ad cost, payback slips past 2030
Payback by 2030 needs average ACoS below 28.6%, barely above the pilot's 28%
The planning team applies the hero product's per-unit economics to all SKUs; duty is 15% of ex-factory cost
A 25% tariff would add $0.35 of duty a unit, 7% of contribution
Repeat purchase (29%) trails the US first-year benchmark (31%)
Two of three Amazon-first K-beauty entrants stayed below $5M of US revenue; execution decided
Competitor evidence: a sample of four brands, so a pattern, not a rate
We read the ambition 'on the way to $40M revenue by 2030' as $40M of US revenue in 2030
Review triggers are our recommendation; the board sets the final thresholds
The 1.3x Amazon halo in Option B rests on a 0.71 correlation across 30 brands, not on cause
next_steps: Approve Option A, the four guardrails and the two retail gates; restate $40M as a post-2030 goal — CEO and board — March 2027

Re-run the cash model on the US tariff decision and set the 2028 ad budget against the ACoS guardrail — CFO — Mid-2027
Report ACoS, 90-day repeat and cumulative cash to the board every quarter — US launch lead — From Q3 2027
